meta.notes: Torah #243 has no edges in torahData.js. All entries below are from source text gap analysis only. The full Torah text is 4 lines. The Rebbe uses the word 'בְּחִינוֹת' explicitly once (line 2), establishing the core bechina of this teaching.

additions.reason: The Tzaddik Gadol is the primary subject of the teaching. His defining characteristic — holiness so extreme that the world cannot bear it, causing him to appear non-holy — is the exact same essential nature as Shir HaShirim's nature as Kodesh Kadashim. The Rebbe uses 'וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת' to make this equation explicit.
additions.source_quote: יֵשׁ צַדִּיק גָּדוֹל מְאֹד, שֶׁאֵין הָעוֹלָם יָכוֹל לִסְבֹּל קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ, עַל־כֵּן הוּא מִתְעַלֵּם מְאֹד, וְאֵין רוֹאִים מִמֶּנּוּ שׁוּם קְדֻשָּׁה וּפְרִישׁוּת יְתֵרָה

additions.reason: Shir HaShirim is the bechina-partner of the Tzaddik Gadol. Both are the supreme instance of their category (the holiest Tzaddik; the holiest book), and both lack visible markers of their holiness. The Rebbe's argument is that Shir HaShirim's absence of the words 'kodesh' and 'tahor' is a direct bechina of the Tzaddik's invisible holiness.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה בְּחִינוֹת: כָּל הַשִּׁירִים קֹדֶשׁ, וְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים... וְזֶה מֵחֲמַת גֹּדֶל עֹצֶם קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ אֵינָם רוֹאִים שָׁם שׁוּם קְדֻשָּׁה

additions.reason: Kodesh Kadashim is the superlative degree of holiness — the name given to Shir HaShirim in the Mishnah (Yadaim 3). It characterizes the nature of the package: holiness that is highest-of-the-high, beyond ordinary degrees. The Rebbe cites this as the reason no explicit holiness-words appear there.
additions.source_quote: כָּל הַשִּׁירִים קֹדֶשׁ, וְשִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים

additions.reason: Concealment (העלם) is the structural outcome of extreme holiness in both cases: the Tzaddik 'hides' (מִתְעַלֵּם), and Shir HaShirim 'hides' its holiness (no words of kodesh or tahor appear). The concealment is not evil or neutral — it is the positive signature of supreme holiness. It belongs to the good package as the very expression of the Tzaddik's and Shir HaShirim's transcendent nature.
additions.source_quote: הוּא מִתְעַלֵּם מְאֹד, וְאֵין רוֹאִים מִמֶּנּוּ שׁוּם קְדֻשָּׁה... וְזֶה מֵחֲמַת גֹּדֶל עֹצֶם קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ אֵינָם רוֹאִים שָׁם שׁוּם קְדֻשָּׁה

additional_context_nodes_not_bechina: משלי וקהלת — mentioned as the contrasting books that DO contain words of holiness/purity; they serve as the foil for Shir HaShirim but are not equated to the Tzaddik via bechina language; they belong to a different conceptual register (ordinary holiness, visible holiness)

קדשה וטהרה (the absent words) — the specific words 'kodesh' and 'tahor' are pointed to as markers of ordinary holiness; their absence is the proof of superlative holiness; they are not bechina-nodes themselves but indicators
analysis_notes.structural_note: Torah #243 has a deliberately minimal structure: one bechina equating the Tzaddik Gadol with Shir HaShirim. The Torah is an aphorism, not a multi-stage argument. There is no eitza chain connecting packages — this Torah is a single package with no evil mirror (the teaching is entirely about the positive domain of supreme holiness). The absence of an evil mirror is itself significant: this teaching describes holiness so pure it has no counterpart in the negative domain within this text.
